Hi Daniel — great to hear you found the demo useful. I took a pass with Ben on a couple of pricing scenarios and put high-level guidance below.

Summary bullets (short):
- Pay-as-you-go (metered): simplest to start, charges per GB retained (hot/nearline) + per-M span ingestion for tracing. Good for pilots.
- 12-month commit (slab + credits): you get a volume discount and a buffer of overage credits per quarter; credits roll forward within the commitment year but do not typically carry across contract years.
- Seat-based dashboards: optional — recommend 15 seats for product + SRE in pilot, otherwise enable via per-user seat licensing.

Hey Daniel — quick technical note on sampling and pilot recommendations:

- For Kubernetes-heavy fleets, per-span pricing is generally more predictable; we typically recommend a combination: 100% ingest for error and high-fidelity traces + 10–20% sampling for low-priority spans.
- Pilot suggestion: 90-day pilot with a capped commit at 1.25x observed usage during the pilot, with a one-time reconciliation at pilot end. This reduces commercial risk and gives you real usage data for an annual commit.
- Retention policy: keep 30 days hot, archive older traces to nearline (cheaper), and provide audit exports for compliance (12-month archive available on request).

If procurement needs the 60-day signature-to-start window, we can accommodate that in the SOW but we usually cap the hold window to 90 days.

-Marissa
